message:
Handoff from Alpha Co to Beta Co.
Message from W2 (Alpha Co refunds worker): "Refunds are done."
Refunds reported as applied: [{"order_id": 161, "amount_cents": 6723}, {"order_id": 163, "amount_cents": 12727}]
The batch is now with you.

reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need to check that the refunds table matches what Alpha reported (order 161 for 6723 and order 163 for 12727). Listing refunds first.
The refunds table matches Alpha's report exactly (orders 161 and 163, with the same amounts), so I can proceed. Next I need the list of orders to identify the customers to pay.
The refunds table matches Alpha's report, so I can proceed. The orders list shows three customers (acme, birch, cobalt). I'll get each customer's net balance from net_balance, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance came back as 46023, which matches its orders (39605 + 19145) minus the refund on order 163 (12727). Next I'll get birch's net balance.
Birch's net balance of 4970 matches its orders (7280 + 4413) minus the refund on order 161 (6723). Cobalt is the last customer, so I'll get its net balance next.

Refunds match Alpha's report, and all three net balances agree with the order and refund amounts. Cobalt's 35816 matches its orders (33787 + 2029) with no refunds. I'll record the payouts now, starting with acme.
Acme's payout of 46023 was recorded successfully. Birch is next, with a net balance of 4970 that I already verified against its orders and refund.
Acme and birch are paid. Cobalt is the last customer, with a net balance of 35816 that I already checked against its orders and the absence of refunds, so I'll record that payout.
All three payouts were recorded successfully. The refunds matched Alpha's report, and each net balance matches its orders minus refunds, so the batch is complete.
